resources.string: Control any app with the S Pen button.

Lets PenScroll perform scroll, tap and swipe gestures in any app when you use the S Pen button, the Quick Settings tile or a recorded macro. It does not read screen content; it only notes which app is open, so it can stop scrolling when you switch apps and pick that app\'s macro.
Turn on PenScroll in Accessibility settings first
Long-press the pen button, then click it with the pen away from the screen.
Also adjustable with − / + on the floating bar.
Page by page (tap edge, for e-readers)
Record taps and swipes for an app, then replay them with pen clicks.
Runs one step (next click runs the next)
Plays the whole macro (click to pause / resume)
No macros yet. Open an app, turn Pen remote on and tap ⏺ on the floating bar.

PenScroll needs Accessibility access to scroll and tap for you.

PenScroll lets the S Pen button scroll and tap in any app.

• Long-press the pen button to turn Pen remote on.
• Click, double-click or triple-click to scroll, turn pages or run a macro.
• A floating bar shows what's happening and lets you adjust or stop.

Touching the screen, switching apps or turning the screen off stops scrolling.

Samsung only lets other apps use the pen's long-press, so PenScroll uses it to turn Pen remote on.

While Pen remote is on, PenScroll shows a media notification and Air actions sends your clicks to it as media buttons (click = play/pause, double-click = next). A click shortly after a double-click counts as a triple-click.

Your music app's pen controls are paused meanwhile; play music once to hand them back. Turning the screen off, long-pressing again, or tapping "Turn off" in the notification ends Pen remote.

Apps with their own pen actions (e.g. Camera) keep the clicks for themselves: turn them off under Settings → Advanced features → S Pen → Air actions.

• Start / stop auto-scroll: scrolls in the style and speed set on the Scroll tab.
• Swipe one page: one swipe of about 60% of the screen per click.
• Reverse direction: flips the scroll direction (or the direction the next click goes).
• Jump to top / bottom: jumps in the current direction; afterwards the direction flips.
• Faster / Slower: changes the speed (or the page interval).

The floating bar shows the current direction as an arrow.

• Continuous: a smooth drag at the chosen speed.
• Page by page (swipe): one no-fling swipe every few seconds.
• Page by page (tap edge): taps the right edge (left when going up) every few seconds, for e-readers.

The interval applies to the page styles. Start / stop auto-scroll, the Quick Settings tile and long-press (when set to scrolling) use this style.

Recording
1. Open the app and long-press the pen button to turn Pen remote on.
2. Tap ⏺ on the floating bar.
3. Each touch becomes a step: tap, long-press (hold ½ s) or swipe. It's also performed on the app, so you can move through its screens. Back and Home are on the toolbar.
4. Tap Save.

Playing
In that app, long-press cycles: off → macro mode → scroll mode → off.
Click = next step (or play / pause with auto-play), double-click = previous step, triple-click = back to step 1.

A macro stays with its app until it finishes, so steps that open the camera keep working.

Waits
Auto-play waits before each step as long as you did while recording. Tap a step below to change its wait.

1. Accessibility → Installed apps → PenScroll → On.
2. Settings → Advanced features → S Pen → Air actions → On.
3. "Hold down Pen button to" → choose PenScroll.
4. Settings → Notifications → Notification access → allow Air command.
5. Allow PenScroll's notification permission when asked.

If Android blocks step 1 for a sideloaded app: App info → ⋮ → Allow restricted settings, then try again.
